title: The Lips That Talk Back
body:
15 Minutes w/ The Captains · 2026-04-01

Opens [Titus 2](/bible/titus/2) · [Eccl 10](/bible/ecclesiastes/10) · [Job 9](/bible/job/9) · [Luke 10](/bible/luke/10) · [Prov 10](/bible/proverbs/10) · [Sir 20](/bible/sirach/20) · [1 Sam 25](/bible/1-samuel/25) · [Eccl 5](/bible/ecclesiastes/5) · [Phil 2](/bible/philippians/2) · [Jude 1](/bible/jude/1) · [Num 16](/bible/numbers/16) · [Sir 21](/bible/sirach/21) · [Matt 12](/bible/matthew/12) · [Sir 28](/bible/sirach/28) · [Luke 6](/bible/luke/6) · [Job 32](/bible/job/32) · and 1 more below
## Introduction *[[0:07](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jilt3SWFtqg&t=7s)]* Today's lesson: the lips that talk back. Talking back is not a small matter. It happened often within Israel. It's a sin that reveals the rebellious in the mind. A lot of times people think talking back would justify them from what you're telling them. ## Scriptures Opened **[Titus 2:9](/bible/titus/2#v9)** *[[0:43](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jilt3SWFtqg&t=43s)]* > [9](/bible/titus/2#v9) Exhort servants to be obedient unto their own masters, and to please them well in all things; not answering again; - Not answering again: it's a lot of brothers' and sisters' kryptonite. They got to answer again. Got to say something. - The mouth reveals what's in the heart. That's what the mouth do. When somebody talk in a conversation, you can know that person wise or you can know that person booked out. **[Ecclesiastes 10:4](/bible/ecclesiastes/10#v4)** *[[1:42](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jilt3SWFtqg&t=102s)]* > [4](/bible/ecclesiastes/10#v4) If the spirit of the ruler rise up against thee, leave not thy place; for yielding pacifieth great offences. - A lot of times in the marriage setting you see this happening a lot. He want to correct his wife, she'll say something. Or she'll say, you're always correcting me. My sister, do you not like correction? You hate correction? Do you not know that he want you to be better? Can't you see the good in what he's saying? But because you have the devil on you, you don't want to hear what he got to say. You want to be correct all the time. You want to be right all the time. That's that Jezebel spirit. He's the head over you. When he say something, see the good in it and better yourself out of it. - Even brothers, when you're working with another brother, your superior, even your peers tell you something, see the good in it and stay in the spirit. - If the spirit of the ruler rise up against thee: that can be the person over you, your husband, your superior, somebody that were leading an event or a project. - Leave not thy place: don't start to argue. Listen and hear what's coming out. - For yielding pacifieth great offences: yielding is the peacemaker. Yielding is not the problematic person. Yielding is the person that want to keep the peace. But a lot of times the mouth gets you in trouble, because you don't know how to just keep quiet and listen and be better. It takes too much energy. It takes too much time. But the justification that you doing take more time than you keeping quiet. - Not talking back allow you to grow. Not making smart remarks, that murmuring, that verbal resistance: all those things is out of order. **[Job 9:20](/bible/job/9#v20)** *[[4:11](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jilt3SWFtqg&t=251s)]* > [20](/bible/job/9#v20) If I justify myself, mine own mouth shall condemn me: if I say, I am perfect, it shall also prove me perverse. - You wonder why you're not better, wonder why you're not growing, because you're always justifying yourself. - If I justify myself: trying to look good and protect that so-called image I think I have, because nobody is above correction. - Mine own mouth shall condemn me: because we all need correction. We all need to be told what to do. It's in the black men and black women in the society: they don't want nobody to tell them what to do, because they have been trained to depend on their own mind. But God's laws and God's guidance, God's structure, is not like that. God's structure is for us to be told what to do. The laws are guidance, tools to get us right. And the laws can be manifest through your leadership, through your husband, through your peers to help you out. - If I say, I am perfect, it shall also prove me perverse: that's why a lot of you sisters and brothers, somebody correct you, you got something to say. They say one, you say two. They say three, you say four. Your mouth is proving that you are perverse. **[Luke 10:25-29](/bible/luke/10#v25)** *[[6:18](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jilt3SWFtqg&t=378s)]* > [25](/bible/luke/10#v25) And, behold, a certain lawyer stood up, and tempted him, saying, Master, what shall I do to inherit eternal life? > > [26](/bible/luke/10#v26) He said unto him, What is written in the law? how readest thou? > > [27](/bible/luke/10#v27) And he answering said, Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy strength, and with all thy mind; and thy neighbour as thyself. > > [28](/bible/luke/10#v28) And he said unto him, Thou hast answered right: this do, and thou shalt live. > > [29](/bible/luke/10#v29) But he, willing to justify himself, said unto Jesus, And who is my neighbour? - Master, what shall I do to inherit eternal life? That's the question he asking Christ. - What is written in the law? how readest thou? Christ asking him a question: do you not read the Bible? You asking how can you get the kingdom? You don't know that it say you got to keep the commandments? - Thou hast answered right: Christ say you answer right. You got it. You know exactly what you need to do. This do, and thou shalt live: I want you to do it, and you going to live. - But he, willing to justify himself, said unto Jesus, And who is my neighbour? Instead of saying, understood, you told me to do it, I will apply. A lot of time people are not like that. They always got something to say. - He wasn't satisfied with what Christ say. The King of kings, Lord of lords tell you do that. The negro say, no, I got to justify myself. That's the spirit in a lot of brothers and sisters. That's why brothers don't grow. That's why sisters don't grow. They think when you tell them something, you coming after them. They think when you advising them, correcting them, you don't like them. Make no sense at all. **[Luke 10:29](/bible/luke/10#v29)** *[[8:38](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jilt3SWFtqg&t=518s)]* > [29](/bible/luke/10#v29) But he, willing to justify himself, said unto Jesus, And who is my neighbour? - A video is shown of a man asked what was the biggest mistake he made during the panel interview that led to him being caught. He answers: "Without a doubt, the biggest mistake I made is that when people told me I did something wrong, I defended myself. Without a doubt, that was my biggest error. And for all the argumentative people out there who will die on a cross defending themselves, take it from me. Just shut the up. Nobody cares about your defense. Once somebody accuses you of something, whether they accuse you of being rude or they accuse you of being selfish or they accuse you of cutting corners or they accuse you of not being serious, once they accuse you, the story in their brain is over. You cannot convince them otherwise. The best thing you can do is to simply acknowledge what they have told you and promise that you will learn from it. The people who succeed at CIA don't succeed because they're perfect. There were people who got certified by the panel who performed worse than I did throughout all of training. The difference was when an instructor went up to them and said, hey, you messed this up, that person said, I did. I'll work on it. I'll get better next time. Whereas when an instructor came up to me and said, Andy, you messed this up, I'd be like, no, no, no. Let me explain what I was thinking. Let me tell you why I did that. Let me show you how smart I am. At the end of the day, nobody wants to work with a person like that." - That's absolutely right. Nobody want to work with somebody that cannot shut up. But he, willing to justify himself: that's it. Sometimes your own mouth will put you in trouble. **[Proverbs 10:19](/bible/proverbs/10#v19)** *[[10:35](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jilt3SWFtqg&t=635s)]* > [19](/bible/proverbs/10#v19) In the multitude of words there wanteth not sin: but he that refraineth his lips is wise. - In the multitude of words: you want to always talk, talk, talk. - There wanteth not sin: sin is going to be part of it, because now you want to justify yourself. Just keep quiet. - But he that refraineth his lips is wise: he that know how to control his spirit. You know how to control your spirit? You are a wise man or woman. **[Sirach 20:5-7](/bible/sirach/20#v5)** *[[11:12](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jilt3SWFtqg&t=672s)]* > [5](/bible/sirach/20#v5) There is one that keepeth silence, and is found wise: and another by much babbling becometh hateful. > > [6](/bible/sirach/20#v6) Some man holdeth his tongue, because he hath not to answer: and some keepeth silence, knowing his time. > > [7](/bible/sirach/20#v7) A wise man will hold his tongue till he see opportunity: but a babbler and a fool will regard no time. - There is one that keepeth silence, and is found wise: why? Because he's observing. He's acting like a sponge. He's soaking everything in and waiting for his ministry, getting built up by those people that's around him. - And another by much babbling becometh hateful: another that talks, talks, talks. Nobody want to sit by that guy. He think he understand everything. He think he know it all. She thinks she know it all. She just want to talk. - Some man holdeth his tongue, because he hath not to answer: some man will hold their tongue because they don't know the answer. They want help. They need help. - And some keepeth silence, knowing his time: he know his time. Read the room. He not just talking, interrupting people. No, he read the room. - A wise man will hold his tongue till he see opportunity: that's why with Nabal, Abigail didn't talk to him immediately. She knew the time. She waited and talked to him the next day. - But a lot of sisters, your lord correct you, right back. He said one, you said two. He said three, you said four. You going at it back to back, back to back. You cannot keep quiet. - But a babbler and a fool will regard no time: one that babble, that just talk, talk, talk. He don't give a damn what time it is. Stop being a damn fool. It's all about themself. They cannot hold their peace. The lips that talk back. **[1 Samuel 25:36](/bible/1-samuel/25#v36)** *[[13:48](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jilt3SWFtqg&t=828s)]* > [36](/bible/1-samuel/25#v36) And Abigail came to Nabal; and, behold, he held a feast in his house, like the feast of a king; and Nabal’s heart was merry within him, for he was very drunken: wherefore she told him nothing, less or more, until the morning light. - Let's go to our reference, Abigail. - She told him nothing, less or more, until the morning light: that's called discretion. You got to have that. You got to be able to read the room. Not every time you will talk. Sometimes your husband do something, your husband say something: now, you got to keep quiet. He correcting you, you keep quiet. You got to be able to stay in the spirit. Somebody correct you, it's for your own good. **[Sirach 20:7-8](/bible/sirach/20#v7)** *[[15:06](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jilt3SWFtqg&t=906s)]* > [7](/bible/sirach/20#v7) A wise man will hold his tongue till he see opportunity: but a babbler and a fool will regard no time. > > [8](/bible/sirach/20#v8) He that useth many words shall be abhorred; and he that taketh to himself authority therein shall be hated. - Stop being a damn fool. People that just want to talk, they call them a babbler and they equal them to a fool. - He that useth many words shall be abhorred: want to talk, talk, talk. He shall be hated. Plain and simple. **[Ecclesiastes 5:1-2](/bible/ecclesiastes/5#v1)** *[[16:06](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jilt3SWFtqg&t=966s)]* > [1](/bible/ecclesiastes/5#v1) Keep thy foot when thou goest to the house of God, and be more ready to hear, than to give the sacrifice of fools: for they consider not that they do evil. > > [2](/bible/ecclesiastes/5#v2) Be not rash with thy mouth, and let not thine heart be hasty to utter any thing before God: for God is in heaven, and thou upon earth: therefore let thy words be few. - Be not rash with thy mouth: rash with your mouth, in all kind of way. - Therefore let thy words be few: that's why we read verse one. It say keep thy foot when thou goest to the house of God, and be more ready to hear than to give the sacrifice of fools: for they consider not that they do evil. So keep in mind the subject matter. When you come to the house of the Lord, you dealing with leadership. Dealing with your brothers and sisters. Dealing with men of rank. Dealing with men that's over you. Be not rash with your mouth. Even your husband, he's over you. Your superior: be not rash with your mouth. - Discretion is a pillar of truth. We got to know how to conduct ourselves. The more someone talk back, the more they are exposed. And it shows pride. It show impatience and it show lack of wisdom. Because wise people know when to speak and when to shut their mouth. They observe the time. So they keep quiet. They are like a sponge. And when the spirit is right, the time is right, then they bring out what they need to bring out. **[Philippians 2:14](/bible/philippians/2#v14)** *[[18:07](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jilt3SWFtqg&t=1087s)]* > [14](/bible/philippians/2#v14) Do all things without murmurings and disputings: - Disputing is an argumentative person. In the house, you arguing, arguing, arguing with your husband. He tell you this, you don't want to listen. Don't do things with disputing and murmuring. **[Jude 1:8](/bible/jude/1#v8)** *[[18:33](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jilt3SWFtqg&t=1113s)]* > [8](/bible/jude/1#v8) Likewise also these filthy dreamers defile the flesh, despise dominion, and speak evil of dignities. - Despise dominion: so they talk back. They despise dominion. They don't like structure. They don't like order. So when you put things in place, they murmur about it. They speak evil about it. - Even it goes down to the house. When a man put things in place, it's up to the woman to keep quiet. He is that dominion. When the Lord made Adam, the Lord gave Adam the dominion. So your husband in the house, he have the dominion in the house. He's the alpha in the house. - And speak evil of dignities: speak evil of leadership. That's what they do. **[Numbers 16:2-4](/bible/numbers/16#v2)** *[[19:43](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jilt3SWFtqg&t=1183s)]* > [2](/bible/numbers/16#v2) And they rose up before Moses, with certain of the children of Israel, two hundred and fifty princes of the assembly, famous in the congregation, men of renown: > > [3](/bible/numbers/16#v3) And they gathered themselves together against Moses and against Aaron, and said unto them, Ye take too much upon you, seeing all the congregation are holy, every one of them, and the Lord is among them: wherefore then lift ye up yourselves above the congregation of the Lord? > > [4](/bible/numbers/16#v4) And when Moses heard it, he fell upon his face: - That was the cliques in verse one: Korah, and Dathan and Abiram, and On, took men. Took cliques. - Two hundred and fifty princes of the assembly, famous in the congregation, men of renown: these men have rank, they have position. - Ye take too much upon you, seeing all the congregation are holy: they say everybody is holy. They say the Lord is among everybody. - And when Moses heard it, he fell upon his face. **[Numbers 16:32](/bible/numbers/16#v32)** *[[21:27](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jilt3SWFtqg&t=1287s)]* > [32](/bible/numbers/16#v32) And the earth opened her mouth, and swallowed them up, and their houses, and all the men that appertained unto Korah, and all their goods. - When people want to go against order, want to talk back, want to murmur against order, then what happened? The earth opened up her mouth. - So all of them that had any part in it, the Lord killed them all. **[Sirach 21:25-26](/bible/sirach/21#v25)** *[[22:19](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jilt3SWFtqg&t=1339s)]* > [25](/bible/sirach/21#v25) The lips of talkers will be telling such things as pertain not unto them: but the words of such as have understanding are weighed in the balance. > > [26](/bible/sirach/21#v26) The heart of fools is in their mouth: but the mouth of the wise is in their heart. - But the words of such as have understanding are weighed in the balance. Very important. - That's what the next verse say: the heart of fools is in their mouth. That's why when men say something or women say something, they are pulling their heart out to you. So when they say nonsense, that's their heart they pulling out to you. - But the mouth of the wise is in their heart: why they say that? The wise taste their words before they bring it out. They taste it first before they bring it out. Plain and simple. **[Matthew 12:36-37](/bible/matthew/12#v36)** *[[23:28](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jilt3SWFtqg&t=1408s)]* > [36](/bible/matthew/12#v36) But I say unto you, That every idle word that men shall speak, they shall give account thereof in the day of judgment. > > [37](/bible/matthew/12#v37) For by thy words thou shalt be justified, and by thy words thou shalt be condemned. - Every idle word that men shall speak, they shall give account thereof in the day of judgment. For by thy words thou shalt be justified, and by thy words thou shalt be condemned. **[Sirach 28:25](/bible/sirach/28#v25)** *[[24:02](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jilt3SWFtqg&t=1442s)]* > [25](/bible/sirach/28#v25) And weigh thy words in a balance, and make a door and bar for thy mouth. - And weigh thy words in a balance: weigh your words in the balance. - And make a door and bar for thy mouth. **[Luke 6:45](/bible/luke/6#v45)** *[[24:41](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jilt3SWFtqg&t=1481s)]* > [45](/bible/luke/6#v45) A good man out of the good treasure of his heart bringeth forth that which is good; and an evil man out of the evil treasure of his heart bringeth forth that which is evil: for of the abundance of the heart his mouth speaketh. - So the things that's evil that come out that you display is that talking back, those smart remarks, that murmuring, and that verbal resisting against God's laws and against structure. **[Job 32:1](/bible/job/32#v1)** *[[25:17](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jilt3SWFtqg&t=1517s)]* > [1](/bible/job/32#v1) So these three men ceased to answer Job, because he was righteous in his own eyes. - Let me show you something. These three men ceased to answer Job, because he was righteous in his own eyes. **[Job 32:4](/bible/job/32#v4)** *[[25:48](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jilt3SWFtqg&t=1548s)]* > [4](/bible/job/32#v4) Now Elihu had waited till Job had spoken, because they were elder than he. - Now Elihu had waited till Job had spoken, because they were elder than he. - So respect got to come in it. We got to be mindful how we deal. The lips that talk back, it cause you to look like a fool, it cause you to look like you don't have no wisdom, it cause you to look really, really foolish. **[Judges 18:19](/bible/judges/18#v19)** *[[26:35](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jilt3SWFtqg&t=1595s)]* > [19](/bible/judges/18#v19) And they said unto him, Hold thy peace, lay thine hand upon thy mouth, and go with us, and be to us a father and a priest: is it better for thee to be a priest unto the house of one man, or that thou be a priest unto a tribe and a family in Israel? - Sometimes this is what we got to do. Hold thy peace: sometimes you talking too much, you need somebody to tell you this. - Lay thine hand upon thy mouth: that's what the scripture say, make a bar for your mouth. Sometimes you don't got to talk back. Sometimes you don't have to talk back at all. - Sometimes you just got to hold your peace, brothers and sisters, and lay your hand over your mouth, because nobody trying to cause you to sin. Your husband want to better you up. Leadership want to better you up. The lips that talk back, it makes us look silly. We need to stop doing that. **[Ecclesiastes 10:4](/bible/ecclesiastes/10#v4)** *[[27:57](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jilt3SWFtqg&t=1677s)]* > [4](/bible/ecclesiastes/10#v4) If the spirit of the ruler rise up against thee, leave not thy place; for yielding pacifieth great offences. - We end it right there. So that's the takeaway, Israel. If some of your husbands mad at you, he's correcting you, don't move from your place. For yielding, for you staying in the spirit, it pacify great offences. You getting corrected, you got to stay in the spirit. He that cannot rule his spirit is like a city without walls. You must be able to rule your spirit so that offence can be pacified, so you can learn from that. - We are not always right at all. So we need brothers and sisters to be real with us. That's how we going to grow. ## In Closing *[[28:57](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jilt3SWFtqg&t=1737s)]* I pray you glean something from that lesson. Brothers stay in the spirit, sisters stay in the spirit. Let's all grow together. Most High and Christ bless. Shalom. --- [15 Minutes Index](/captains) · [Watch the full session on YouTube ↗](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jilt3SWFtqg)
